newsitem.title: USA: James River set to battle Kimberly after deal.
newsitem.headline: James River set to battle Kimberly after deal.

text.p: The proposed union of James River Corp and Fort Howard Corp will create a diversified company with less exposure to the cyclical paper sector and more muscle to battle Kimberly-Clark Corp.
Industry experts said the union will combine James River's strong consumer market position with Fort Howard's commercial presence and state-of-the-art facilities.
"I think it's something that James River had to do. It gives them a much stronger base to compete," said one investment banker who did not want to be identified.

The two companies announced earlier Monday they planned to merge in a stock transaction that values Fort Howard shares at about $42 each. The companies called the formation of the new Fort James Corp a merger of equals, but most of Wall Street viewed it as James River's acquisition of Fort Howard.

Although James River already holds the number two spot with brands like Quilted Northern toilet tissue and Brawny paper towels, the Richmond, Va.-based company would now be much closer in size to Kimberly-Clark.
At a press conference to discuss the merger, company executives stressed the consumer market potential of the deal.

"Our new entity truly pushes forward the grand opportunities that lie ahead of us for worldwide growth. These two companies are ready to emerge as a powerful single force and industry leader in paper-based consumer groups," James River chief executive officer Miles Marsh said at a press conference to discuss the merger.

At the press conference, the two companies said the new firm will use Fort Howard's technology to develop new brands and expand into new markets. Industry experts said Fort Howard's key strength lies in the recycled paper business.
Officials of both companies said they are hopeful the deal can be concluded without any asset sales. They also said they hope the deal will be completed by the end of the summer.

Despite that optimism, shares of Fort Howard traded below the announced deal price of $42.45 per share due to concerns that the deal may not pass federal muster within the timeframe set by the companies.

The transaction is likely to be closely scrutinized by the U.S. Department of Justice, which required divestitures before it approved the $9.4 billion union of Kimberly-Clark and Scott Paper Co in 1995.
By mid-afternoon, Fort Howard shares were trading at 41-3/4, up 5-1/4 from Friday's close. James River stock was up 1-1/4 at 32-1/8.
"Office Depot has put the fear of God into everybody," one takeover trader said, referring to the government's opposition to a proposed merger of Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc.
